nodes.notes:
Monitoring and Controlling - Chapter 8

Monitoring and Controlling

Expert Judgement - Your own intuition

Main tool and technique for monitoring and controlling

Earned Value Management

Measures project performance based on scope, schedule, and cost

Planned Value (PV)- Portion of approved total cost estimate that was planned to have been spent during a given period

Actual Costs (AC) - Total costs that were actually incurred

Rate of Performance (RP) - Amount of work completed as a proportion of work expected to be completed at given time

Earned Value (EV) - Estimate of the value of work performed in given period



Calculations

Cost Variance (CV) - Compared budgeted cost vs actual costs



Schedule Variance (SV) - Compared work performed vs actual work performed 

SV = EV - PV

Cost Performance Index - Financial effectiveness of a project

CPI = EV / AC

> 1 is good

Schedule Performance Index - How close the project is to schedule

SPI = EV / PV

> 1 is good

Estimate at Completion - Best guess for how much money will be spent at the end of the project

Project Scope Management

Scope Creep - tendency of scope to increase over time

Wasa Video

Wasa - a warship

Changes

Speed up ship

Increase to 120 feet

Changed to 111

Needed double cannons

Needed much more space

Died of a heart attack after all changes

Ship sunk after 15 minutes

Project Schedule Management

Know the status of the schedule

Influence the factors that can cause schedule issues

Determine whether the schedule has changed

Manage changes when they occur

Slipped Milestone - A milestone reached later than expected

What do sponsors hate most?

Surprises

Be clear and honest with sponsors 

Control Charts - Illustrate results of a process over time

Seven Run Rule - Examine if there is a problem if there are 7 data points in a row above/below mean

Pareto Chart - Bar chart with cumulative percentage as line

80%/20% rule - 80% of problems come from 20% of causes

Stratification - separate data to see patterns

Project Risk Management

Workarounds - Unplanned responses to risk events 

Project Procurement Management

Constructive Change Orders - Oral or written requests made by someone with authority

Project Cost Management

To-Complete Performance Index



Examples



Closing Projects - Chapter 9 

Closing

Closing Methods

Integration - Project completed successfully, integrated into operations

Most common

Addition - New unit added to company as result of project

Extinction - Project done, no addition or integration

Extinction by murder - Higher up kills project

Starvation - Project ends by stopping funding

Withdrawal of life support

Outputs

Transition plan - Final product, processes, and instructions to use them

Lessons Learned Report - Major takeaways for a future project

Close-out Meeting

Opposite of a kickoff meeting

Includes major stakeholders

Knowledge Transfer - Sharing of knowledge gained during project

Employee knowledge, human capital, is the key asset of company

Challenger

Failure with O-Ring

People at lower levels could not communicate with top levels

nodes.name: Challenger
nodes.excerpt: Challenger is a case study highlighting communication failures in project management.
nodes.notes: The Challenger case study illustrates the failure of communication between lower and top levels, leading to a critical failure with the O-Ring. It emphasizes the importance of effective communication in project management.

nodes.name: Closing Projects
nodes.excerpt: Closing Projects involves methods like integration, addition, extinction, and starvation.
nodes.notes: Closing Projects is the final phase in project management, involving methods such as integration, addition, extinction, and starvation. It includes outputs like a transition plan, lessons learned report, and a close-out meeting.

nodes.name: Earned Value Management
nodes.excerpt: Earned Value Management measures project performance based on scope, schedule, and cost.
nodes.notes: Earned Value Management is a technique used in project management to measure project performance. It involves calculations like Planned Value (PV), Actual Costs (AC), Rate of Performance (RP), and Earned Value (EV). It helps in determining Cost Variance (CV), Schedule Variance (SV), Cost Performance Index (CPI), and Schedule Performance Index (SPI).

nodes.name: Monitoring and Controlling
nodes.excerpt: Monitoring and Controlling involves expert judgement and earned value management.
nodes.notes: Monitoring and Controlling is a key concept in project management, involving the use of expert judgement and tools like Earned Value Management to measure project performance based on scope, schedule, and cost.

nodes.name: Project Procurement Management
nodes.excerpt: Project Procurement Management involves handling constructive change orders.
nodes.notes: Project Procurement Management deals with the acquisition of goods and services from external sources. It includes managing constructive change orders, which are oral or written requests made by someone with authority.

nodes.name: Project Risk Management
nodes.excerpt: Project Risk Management involves planning for and responding to risk events.
nodes.notes: Project Risk Management is about identifying, assessing, and responding to risks. It includes planning for workarounds, which are unplanned responses to risk events.

nodes.name: Project Schedule Management
nodes.excerpt: Project Schedule Management involves knowing and influencing the schedule status and changes.
nodes.notes: Project Schedule Management focuses on understanding the status of the schedule, influencing factors that can cause schedule issues, determining changes, and managing them effectively. It includes concepts like slipped milestones and the importance of clear communication with sponsors.

nodes.name: Project Scope Management
nodes.excerpt: Project Scope Management involves managing scope creep and ensuring project scope is controlled.
nodes.notes: Project Scope Management is crucial in controlling the tendency of scope to increase over time, known as scope creep. It involves understanding and managing the project scope effectively to avoid unnecessary changes.

nodes.name: Wasa Video
nodes.excerpt: Wasa Video is a case study of the warship Wasa, illustrating project management failures.
nodes.notes: The Wasa Video is a case study that discusses the warship Wasa, which underwent numerous changes such as speeding up the ship, increasing its size, and adding double cannons, leading to its sinking after 15 minutes. It highlights the consequences of unmanaged scope changes.
